analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/reference/configuration.md (changed range head 393-395) and a new report docs/reports/2026-10-21-mixed-step-prefill-geometry.md. It adds and revises env-var docs for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK, DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE, and records the 2048/4096 prefill geometry measurements. The diff contains no executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption or coordinator-contract changes.

Security-relevant observations:
- The docs state that the wide prefill geometry (Gemma 4 default) raises activation peaks. For GPT-OSS at 32k it reaches 0.12 GiB beyond its floor, and Qwen3.5-9B reaches 0.53 GiB beyond its default. Only Gemma 4 takes the wide geometry by default, with at least 1.77 GiB of margin, so the documented defaults keep the risky models on the old geometry. This is an availability and memory-pressure consideration (provider DoS or OOM), not a confidentiality regression. The source change that makes Gemma 4 default to wide and applies the media ceiling lives in provider-swift files not supplied here, so I could not verify that the code matches the docs.
- The report notes p99 and max inter-token gaps grow 2-3x under the wide geometry, which is a latency tradeoff.
- The report notes that no load arm used repeated prefixes, so it makes no claim touching the T-041 prefix-cache timing oracle. The mention of dense Qwen recurrent checkpoints every 2048 tokens under the opt-in is performance only. No claim in the docs weakens prefix-cache scoping, TTL, encryption or the SEC-035 posture.
- The new env controls are process-scoped and are not claimed to be LaunchAgent-forwarded in the changed text.

The rest of configuration.md is unchanged context. It was read for consistency and has no new attack surface.

Remaining question for integration: the code behind the new Gemma 4 default (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift) should be reviewed for memory-admission interaction with the activation floors. It is outside this batch.
